followups.problem: compareStageIds is case-sensitive (/^S(\d+)$/ without the i flag), but the new compareStageCategoryNames (cockpit-lists.js:35) is case-insensitive. So the two stage comparators disagree. The stage-count span (.stripl .st, cockpit-view.js:218), the 'N OF M STAGES DONE' count and the strip segment order all come from stageRingProgress, which uses compareStageIds.
followups.exploit_or_failure: If a ledger records stage ids in lowercase (scope.stages or ticket.stage = s1..s11), the stack sub-line now reads s1 / s2 / ... / s11, but the stage-count span reads 's1 0/1 · s10 0/1 · s11 0/1 · s2 0/1 ...' because those ids fail the regex and fall back to localeCompare. This is the same kind of bug the owner reported, on the line next to the fixed one. The new test uses uppercase S ids, so it does not catch this.
followups.fix: Add the i flag in compareStageIds (/^S(\d+)$/i). Better still, export one comparator from cockpit-lists.js and use it in both places. Then add a lowercase-id variant of the new mounted test, or parameterise it over case.

followups.problem: The page-wide leaf scan only checks a list if the whole list is inside one leaf element's text. The category legend (cockpit-view.js:222-230) puts each stage name in its own <b> sibling inside .lg, so every leaf holds one id and the scan skips it. The legend order is only tested indirectly, because it shares cats.names with the stack sub-line. The CHANGELOG/test claim that every stage list on the page is covered is too strong.
followups.exploit_or_failure: If the legend were later built from a different source (for example rings, or a re-sorted copy), it could show S1 S10 S9 ... and this test would still pass.
followups.fix: Also check the joined text of the legend: assert stagesNumericOrder(textOf(host.querySelector('.stripl .lg'))). Or scan any element whose direct children are leaves, using its combined text.

summary: The fix is correct for the owner-reported bug. cockpitCategories (cockpit-lists.js:87) sorts names only when field === 'stage', after the ticket-id-order collection, so lane/area/type order is byte-for-byte unchanged. Sorting only for stage is right: other fields are free-form labels whose ticket-order grouping is intentional. Names are already trimmed and lowercased by ticketCategory, and the comparator matches case-insensitively, breaks numeric ties (s01 vs s1) by localeCompare and puts non-S ids last, which is deterministic. The comparator is a valid total order, so Array.sort is stable. The stack sub-line (cc-cockpit-mount.js:692-693), the legend (cockpit-view.js:224) and the in-segment grouping (cockpit-view.js:245/256) all read cats.names, so they all follow the new order. With field=stage each strip segment holds one stage, and segment order comes from stageRingProgress. The new test is not tautological: with the old code, tickets T-01..T-11 carrying S1,S10,S9,S8,S11,S2..S7 give the sub-line 's1 / s10 / s9 / s8 / s11 / s2 ...', and stagesNumericOrder fails at 10 followed by 9. The fixture has no lane/area/type, so the stage field is chosen. Its scope.stages are scrambled, so the stage-count span assertion also exercises compareStageIds. The other changes are only version pins (package.json, package-lock.json, README, CHANGELOG, 6 release-pin tests), consistent with 1.167.37, and none are unrelated. Two non-blocking followups: compareStageIds is still case-sensitive, so lowercase ledger stage ids would misorder the stage-count span; and the leaf scan does not see lists split across sibling elements (the legend). Limits: I did not run tests (no shell). The review is based on the diff and the listed files only.
